context.purpose: U6 universe-cycle parallel-scaling MECHANISM proof on real OPRA
context.host: i7-1260p (4 P-cores + 8 E-cores; 16 logical); pricing executor pinned to P-cores
context.pipeline: load_opra_daterange -> corpus_board_from_opra -> populate_surface_db (U1 streaming per-date release + U2 LPT claim order + U3 date-granular durability + U4 shared small-book budget, over the E2 work-stealing pool)
context.method: best-of-3 (Repetitions=3, Iterations=1), median reported; inner per-board fit pinned to 1 thread (ATX_VOL_FIT_WORKERS=1) so the sweep isolates OUTER board-level parallelism (populate n_threads) and Sum(board_ms) is invariant.
context.eff_cores_def: eff_cores(P) = fit_ms(1) / fit_ms(P) = board-level fit-stage speedup
findings: Monotone speedup 1.00 -> 3.83x across P=1..8; near-ideal at low P (par_eff 0.86 @ P=2).
Peak RSS bounded: 55.6 -> 67.1 MB for 8x workers (streaming per-date release; O(dates-in-flight), not O(all dates)).

Beyond 8 threads the curve plateaus/regresses (P=12: 8.9s, P=16: 7.2s > P=8: 6.9s): the box has only 4 physical P-cores, so 3.83x at 8 threads is near-linear PER PHYSICAL P-CORE; extra E-cores are slower and oversubscribe on a 33-board skewed cohort.

The >=6 eff-cores / wall(1)/wall(12)>=6 north-star gate needs >=6 PHYSICAL performance cores AND the 519-name cohort (board-count >> worker-count) -- both data- and hardware-gated on this laptop. MECHANISM (monotone, near-linear-per-P-core, bounded RSS) proven.
